From: Amir Qureshi <amir.qureshi@brightlane.com>

Date: 2026-10-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Maintenance calendar alignment & SLA response-time redlines

Connor — thanks for the walkthrough this morning. Ellen and I reviewed the draft MSA + order form and we have three primary items we'd like to see addressed before legal will sign: uptime target, service credit cap, and P1 response window. High-level asks below; annotated redlines attached (Brightlane_SLA_redlines_v3.pdf).

1) Uptime: current doc calls out 99.9% monthly. Given Brightlane's customer experience needs, we're asking to move to 99.95% (or define a ladder with 99.95 minimum for core endpoints).
2) Service credits: we're pushing against an unlimited lookback; request a 12-month lookback cap and a hard cap at 50% of monthly fees per incident (we'd prefer 25%-50% range).
3) Response times: P1 response currently 1 hour. For our SLOs we need initial acknowledgement within 30 minutes and remediation ETA within 2 hours for system-wide outages.

Operationally, maintenance windows: we'd like a clearer recurring maintenance window (weekend preferred). Can you confirm Redwood's proposed blackout/maintenance calendar and whether planned maintenance can be scheduled outside Brightlane's peak hours? I attached a proposed calendar (maintenance_windows_calendar.ics) with weekend windows.

If we can close on these items this week, procurement can finalize payment terms next week and we can push to a Nov 1 start.

Thanks — Amir

Priority items for legal:

- Credit cap and lookback window (they're proposing 12 months / 25-50% per incident).
- Explicit carveouts: planned maintenance, force majeure, customer-caused incidents.

Connor — thanks for the ping. I reviewed Brightlane's annotated redlines and drafted prioritized language for the following items. I've attached an annotated PDF with inline comments (Brightlane_SLA_redlines_v3.pdf). Summary below — high level suggestions and the legal trade-offs.

1) Uptime: Recommend keeping a two-tier ladder rather than a single 99.95 threshold. Suggested language: "Core API endpoints: 99.95% monthly; Non-core endpoints: 99.9% monthly. Failure to meet Core API uptime will trigger the credit ladder below." Rationale: this preserves higher guarantee where it matters while limiting exposure on non-core traffic.

2) Service credits & caps: Counterproposal: 12-month lookback window (OK), credit ladder as: 99.95–99.9 => 5% credit; 99.9–99.0 => 15% credit; <99.0 => 30% credit for the affected month. Hard cap: credits for any single month limited to 50% of monthly fees; aggregate annual credit cap at 100% of a single monthly invoice. Rationale: Limits long-tail financial exposure while offering meaningful remediation. Brightlane's ask of a 25% hard cap per incident is higher than we typically accept; propose 50% monthly cap instead of per incident.

3) Response times (P1): I don't object to the 30-minute ACK ask, but we need to define P1 narrowly (system-wide unavailability affecting >50% of requests or production data loss). Proposed fallback language: "Redwood will acknowledge P1 incidents within 30 minutes during business and non-business hours; initial remediation ETA will be communicated within 2 hours. For issues limited to single-tenant or non-core subsystems, Redwood may apply extended acknowledgment windows and ETA timelines as defined in the runbook." This protects us from over-committing.

4) Maintenance windows: If Brightlane requires Sun 02:00-06:00 PT as the recurring window, we can generally accommodate but require: (a) minimum 72-hour notice for planned maintenance; (b) a maximum of 8 hours/month of scheduled maintenance outside emergency patches; (c) a blackout period during their high-traffic days as documented. Also request to include a clause that Redwood will provide one scheduled maintenance blackout per quarter on their request.

Open items: audit log retention (they requested custom retention) and any additional compliance evidence (SOC 2 scope). If Brightlane needs extended retention, that will be a commercial add-on.

Naomi — can you confirm the ops constraints above? Specifically: acknowledgement timeline commitment and the monthly scheduled maintenance cap.

Let me know if you want me to push any of these items as firm positions or as negotiable. I'm happy to present as a counterproposal to keep negotiations moving.

Laura Bennett

Connor / Laura — appreciate the fast turnaround and proposed language. Ellen and I reviewed Laura's counterproposal and we're generally aligned on the ladder approach for uptime. Two points before we can sign:

1) Credit cap: Laura's 50% monthly cap is reasonable, but Brightlane requests that the annual aggregate cap be at least 150% of monthly fees (we can't accept only 100% annual cap). Can you confirm if Redwood can move to 150% aggregate cap?
2) Maintenance slot: we can accept the 72-hour notice and the 8 hours/month cap as long as Redwood confirms the recurring slot Sun 02:00-06:00 PT is reserved for Brightlane and not used for other customer-impacting maintenance that would reduce our availability in that window.

If Redwood can accept those two items, we can issue the PO and route the order form to our procurement team for signature. Proposed timeline: finalize redlines today, procurement sign-off tomorrow, invoice/PO issuance by Oct 24.

Thanks — Amir
